pool.text: Calais became part of the county of Boulogne after a town charter was granted.
Richard the Lionheart landed at Calais on his journey to the Third Crusade.
Edward III of England captured Calais, bringing the city under English control.
The Treaty of Brétigny assigned Calais to English rule in perpetuity.
France recaptured Calais, ending a long period of English control.
A Zeppelin bombardment smashed the stained glass of the church.
The historic watch tower has been classified as a historic monument.
German forces invaded and took the strategic bombing target during a siege.
The Todt Organisation built a former Nazi bunker and wartime military headquarters.
Massive bunkers were built along the coast in preparation for launching missiles.
General Daniel Spry's 3rd Canadian Infantry Division laid siege to and liberated the town.
Royal Air Force bombers mistook Calais for Dunkirk during a final bombing raid.
The Chemin de fer d'Anvin à Calais closed down completely.
Calais was officially twinned with the city of Duisburg in Germany.
Calais formed a twinning relationship with the city of Wismar, Germany.
Calais established a twinning partnership with Dover in the United Kingdom.
The 55-metre-high tower was automated by authorities.
The Channel Tunnel has connected Calais and Folkestone.
Calais became twinned with the city of Brăila located in Romania.
Calais established a twinning connection with Bardejov situated in Slovakia.
